stem: Which of the following matches is not correct regarding the origin of Harappan civilization?

options.label: a
options.text: M. Rafi que Mughal - Harappan civilization was inspired by Mesopotamian civilization

options.label: b
options.text: E.J.H. Mackay - Migration of people from Sumer

options.label: c
options.text: Mortimer Wheeler - Migration of the idea of civilization from Western Asia

options.label: d
options.text: Amalandanda Ghosh - Pre-Harappan culture matured to make Harrapan civilization

expl: About the origin of the Harappan civilization, many scholars have presented diff erent views. E.J.H. Mackay has considered that the origin of the Harappan civilization was due to the migration of people from Sumer (Mesopotamia), while historians D.H. Gordon and Mortimer Wheeler considered that the Harappan civilization was the result of migration of the idea of civilization from Western Asia. In this context, Amalananda Ghosh considered that pre-Harappan culture matured into Harappan civilization. M.F. Rafi que Mughal considered that the development of Harappan civilization occurred in the region of Ravi river at Harappa. He refutes the old belief that Harappan civilization was inspired by Mesopotamian civilization.

stem: Which colour was commonly used in the Harappan Pottery?
expl: The Harappan pottery is bright or dark red and uniformly sturdy and well baked. It consists of wheel-made wares, both plain and painted. The plain ware is usually of red clay with or without a fi ne red slip. The painted pottery was of red and black colours. Several methods were used by people for the decoration of pottery. Polychrome pottery was rare and mainly comprised small vases decorated with geometric patterns, mostly in red, black and green and less frequently in white and yellow. The colour- scheme adopted for painting was light black, chocolate or light red over buff or greenish buff background.

stem:
Based on findings of excavation of Harappan Civilization, what are not true?
(i) For all kinds of constructions, same size of bricks were used.
(ii) Mostly all the houses were single storey.
(iii)Main roads were on average ten meters in width.
expl: In Indus Valley Civilisation both baked and raw bricks were used. Generally the dimensional ratio of burned bricks received from all the Indus towns was 4 : 2 : 1. However ornamental bricks from Kalibangan and curved bricks from Chanhudaro have been found. Hence statement (i) is wrong. Most of the houses built in the Indus Valley Civilisation were built with one storey only, but some houses were also built with two stories as evidence of stairs have been found from some houses. Hence statement (ii) is wrong. The width of roads in Harappan cities was generally 10 meters. Hence statement (iii) is right.

stem: Which one of the following ancient towns is well-known for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channelizing water into connected reservoirs?
expl: Dholavira in Gujarat is well known for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channeling water into connected reservoirs.

stem: A highly advanced water management system of Harappan times has been unearthed at–
expl: From Dholavira, a huge Rock-cut reservoir is found, whose size is about 79 m × 12 m and 7 meters deep, having a huge capacity to store water. People of Dholavira were familiar with the advanced water management system. From the earliest evidence, people used to store water in this reservoir by building dams.

stem: Recently, from excavations of Harappan site Sonauli what was found ?
expl: Sinauli is an archaeological site located in Baraut Tehsil, Baghpat district, Uttar Pradesh, where 125 graves belonging to Indus Valley Civilization were found. These graves are oriented in a North-South direction and most are identifi ed as primary human burials. Some of the burials are found with animal bones and gold, copper and bangles.

stem: In which State of India is the Harappan Civilization site Mandi situated?
expl: Mandi is a village in the Muzaff arnagar district of Uttar Pradesh. It became famous after discovery and loot of an ancient treasure trove by villagers in June 2000. As per ASI, the jewellery found belonged to the late Harappan period.

stem: For clothing, cotton cultivation was fi rst introduced in–
expl: Cotton was first cultivated in India for clothing. In 1922, Rakhal Das Banerjee took an interest in the site of Mohenjo-Daro for excavation. Evidence of the earliest cotton cultivation was found by excavation in India. From India, it reached Greece where it was called “Sindon”. The cotton cultivation in India started in 3000 B.C. while it was cultivated in Egypt in 2500 B.C.

stem:
Which of the following characterizes/characterize the people of Indus Civilization?
1. They possessed great places and temples.
2. They worshipped, both male and female deities.
3. They employed horse-drawn chariots in warfare.
Select the correct answer using the code given below
expl: No temple or place of worship has been found in excavation from Indus Valley Civilization till date. The only religious source from this civilization is statues made of mud and stone and seals which were found here. By this, it is known that female deities, Shiva or Pashupati and animals like snake, elephant were worshipped. Worship of plants and trees, or inanimate stone or other objects in the form of ‘Linga’ or ‘yoni’ symbols was famous during that period.

stem:
Regarding the Indus Valley Civilization, consider the following statements
1. It was predominantly a secular civilization and the religious element, though present, did not dominate the scene.
2. During this period, cotton was used for manufacturing textiles in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Indus Valley Civilization is considered to be a secular civilization with no trace of theocratic or organized religion. Cotton textiles were produced during the Harappan period as shown by artefact evidence.

stem: One of the following sites from where the famous bull-seal of Indus Valley Civilization was found-
expl: Mohenjodaro is an archaeological site in the province of Sindh, Pakistan (excavated by R.D. Banerjee in 1922). From this site, various sculptures, seals, pottery, gold and jewellery have been found. But the most famous among them is the humped bull seal.

stem: The famous female figurine known as 'Dancing Girl', found at Mohenjo-daro, is made of
expl: The world-famous female figurine found at Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilization, is known as the “Dancing Girl.” It is an approximately 10.5-centimetre-high metal figurine, cast using the lost-wax technique. Its metallurgical analysis and archaeological descriptions indicate that it is made of bronze.

stem: The shape of which tree is found in the seals from the Indus Civilization?
expl: Most of the seals discovered from Indus Valley Civilisation were made of steatite. A few of them were also made of terracotta, agate, chert etc. Most of seals were square in shape but few were in cube, circle and cylindrical shapes too. Pipal tree is represented number of times on Indus seals depicting that Pipal had important/sacred value to Indus people.

stem: Which one of the following animals is not depicted on the Harappan seal ?
expl: People of the Harappa civilization were known to horses, but no pieces of evidence have been found on seals. A great majority of seals found in Indus Valley civilization carry short inscriptions with fi gures of the one-horned animal (most common), the Buff alo, the Tiger, the Rhinoceros, the Goat and the Elephant.

stem: Remains of which animal have not been discovered in the Indus Valley Civilization?
expl: Among given options, the evidence of cow and elephant have been found and there is some dispute regarding horse, but the latest excavation has revealed the evidence of horse. The evidence of lion from the excavation of Harappan Civilization has not been mentioned anywhere. Hence,option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
expl: Among the given options evidence of Bull and Elephant have been found. Seal of Zebu Bull has been found. Seals depicting Elephant have also been found. There is some dispute regarding horse but latest excavation has revealed evidence of horse. However, Horses did not play any major role during the Indus Valley Civilisation. BPSC has accepted (b) as correct answer.

stem: According to the report of IIT Kharagpur study group, continuous low rainfall for how many years was the cause of fall of the Indus valley civilization?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the reports of IIT Kharagpur, the continuous low or negligible rainfall for 900 years was the cause of fall of the Indus Valley Civilisation. In other words, it can be said that continuous drought for 900 years led the fall of Indus Valley Civilisation.

stem: A horned deity engraved on a terracotta cake has been recovered from
expl: From excavations at Kalibangan, a series of ‘fi re altars’ on mud-brick platforms were discovered. A triangular terracotta cake found at Kalibangan had a carving of a horned deity on one side and an animal (goat) being dragged by a rope by a human on the other. This shows the way to the emergence of a sacrifi cial tradition in the entire era.

stem: Which of the following civilizations fl ourished on the bank of River Nile ?
expl: Ancient Egyptian Civilization fl ourished along the banks of the River Nile for almost 3,000 years. Nile River is known as the ‘lifeline of Egypt.’ The Nile is a major north-fl owing river in northeastern Africa, generally regarded as the longest river in the world. Indus Valley Civilization (India) and Mesopotamia (Iraq) are the contemporary civilizations.

stem: What is the correct North-South sequence of the following civilizations?
expl: The correct sequence of the following civilizations from North to South is: Aztec - Maya- Muisca - Inca.The expansion of Aztec civilization was on the Northern Part of Mesoamerica. Mesoamerica included the Region from central Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Northern Costa Rica. Mayan civilization was spread over the southern part of Mesoamerica. Moisca civilization was distributed in the eastern part of Columbia (South America continent), whereas Inca civilization is spread in the western part of southern America till the north of Quito and Santiago to the South.

stem: The oldest civilization in the world is
expl: The Mesopotamian civilization is considered the world's oldest civilization. This civilization developed in present-day Iraq and the surrounding areas. The Egyptian civilization (the civilization of the Nile) developed in the Nile River basin and is considered to have emerged after the Mesopotamian civilization.

stem: The fi rst ancient civilization to develop the art of writing in a proper system was?
expl: People of the Sumerian Civilization were the fi rst to develop the art of writing in a proper system. Their primary script was very simple and primitive. Cuneiform script of Sumeria is generally known as one of the earliest systems of writing.
